lines.text: Today you choose your teaching path and build one complete lesson pack with AI, then check it like an examiner.
Path A is a school teacher, path B is a tutor or coaching centre, and path C is a workplace or skills trainer.
Every task today has an example for each path.
Use your own topic, your own learners and your own syllabus.
Give the AI the class or group, the subject, the topic, the time and one clear goal.
Ask for a starter, a main activity, practice and a quick check at the end.
Then shape it to your learners, your board and your own style.
Differentiated means the same topic at different levels: support, core and challenge.
Ask for three short versions of a worksheet, with an answer key and working.
Every learner practises the same idea at the right level.
A rubric shows what good work looks like at each level.
The AI can draft one, and can turn your rough notes into kind, specific feedback.
Use a placeholder instead of the student’s name, and add your own personal touch.
AI answer keys are often wrong, so solve every question yourself.
Check the reading level, the examples and the cultural fit, and match it to your own syllabus.
Students’ names, marks and photos never go into a personal AI account.
A Class 6 teacher asks for one worksheet on adding fractions, at three levels.
The questions are clear, and the word problems use familiar names and situations.
But look at the last core answer: three quarters plus one eighth is not four twelfths.
The right answer is seven eighths, so we solve every answer ourselves before printing.
A tutor turns rough marking notes into feedback a student can act on.
The placeholder means no student name ever goes into the chatbot.
The comment has one strength, one improvement and one next step.
The tutor still reads it for accuracy and adds a personal line before sharing it.
A workplace trainer wants a quiz that comes only from the training handout.
NotebookLM answers from the sources you add, and shows where each answer came from.
Click the citations to check, and still answer every question yourself.
Before any AI material reaches learners, run this six-point check.
Solve every answer, read it as your weakest reader, and check the examples feel familiar.
Match it to your syllabus, and check facts against your own book.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
